source: AI Agent Orchestration September 2026 Survey (dutchstartup.ai + symphony-solutions)
summary: High-level survey of new agent tools appearing September 2026: multi-model cost reduction, persistent memory across sessions, human-in-the-loop governance, and MCP/A2A protocol adoption for enterprise.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — enterprise adoption story with no concrete implementable patterns; themes (memory, governance) already tracked in open issues.

source: Karpathy Agentic Engineering / LLM Wiki (aibuilderclub.com + mindstudio.ai)
summary: Karpathy's 9-rule agentic engineering framework and LLM Wiki paradigm: compile raw materials into persistent Markdown wiki rather than re-deriving on every query; recursive loops with planning, generation, review, and disk-state management.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — agents.md / CLAUDE.md patterns already in use; LLM Wiki paradigm not directly applicable to AgentForge's CLI-subprocess state machine model. No actionable gap.

summary: LangGraph May 2026: DeltaChannel stores only incremental deltas per step instead of full state re-serialization; ContextHubBackend persists agent skills/memories as Hub commits with version history.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — LangGraph-specific features; AgentForge is not LangGraph-based and uses a different state machine model. DeltaChannel pattern not applicable to PostgreSQL/Prisma stack.

source: Lilian Weng — Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement (Lil'Log July 2026)
summary: Synthesis of harness-as-deployment-layer for recursive self-improvement: three design patterns (workflow automation, filesystem as persistent memory, sub-agents/backend jobs), tool surface taxonomy, and a map of self-improving-harness research.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — filesystem-as-persistent-memory pattern maps to AgentForge's artifact model; sub-agent configuration patterns relevant to orchestrator design. However all specific gap themes this touches (episodic memory HID-188, skill distillation) are already tracked. Backlog full this run.

summary: Propose-evaluate-accept loop where LLM agents mine their own execution traces for failure patterns and propose targeted edits to one of 7 harness components (system prompt, tool desc, tool impl, middleware, skill, sub-agent config, long-term memory); changes are validated before acceptance.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — pattern of distilling failures into harness improvements is directionally aligned with AgentForge's skill distillation. However propose-evaluate-accept loop over harness code falls into the RL training loop red flag category from the evaluation criteria. Backlog also full.

source: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents (arxiv 2604.10674)
summary: Skill-conditioned self-distillation: agents learn from their own multi-turn execution traces by distilling successful sub-trajectories into reusable skill templates that condition future rollouts, improving success rate on complex tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to the known gap that executor prompts don't receive distilled skills yet (noted in CLAUDE.md Key Limitations #8). AgentForge already has distillationAgent.ts and agentSkillRepository.ts; the Skill-SD pattern would strengthen the executor skill-injection path currently tracked by HID-188. Backlog full this run.

summary: Framework for preserving agent identity, memory, and code across model changes, harness versions, and server migrations; proposes portable agent bundles with versioned memory snapshots.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — cross-run persistence theme already tracked by HID-188 (inject cross-run episodic memory into planner and executor prompts). Portable agent bundles concept is over-engineered relative to AgentForge's single-service architecture.

source: Delivery, Not Storage: Cue-Anchored Working Memory as Harness Property (arxiv 2607.20972)
summary: Argues working memory for coding agents should be framed as a delivery mechanism (cue-anchored retrieval at the right moment) not a storage problem; harness is responsible for deciding when and what to surface into context.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant to HID-188 (skill/memory injection). The cue-anchoring insight (surface memories at stage boundaries, not as a batch dump) could strengthen the HID-188 implementation design. Not a separate issue; best as a comment on HID-188.

source: AREX: Towards a Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research (arxiv 2607.21461)
summary: AREX proposes recursive self-improvement via RL fine-tuning of the agent policy from its own research traces; combines retrieval, planning, and execution with an automated evaluation loop to drive improvement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — RL fine-tuning loop is explicitly disqualified per evaluation criteria (red flag: RL training loops). Not adoptable in AgentForge's CLI-subprocess architecture without significant infrastructure.

source: Google AX (Agent Orchestration Runtime, GitHub trending Sep 2026)
summary: Google open-sourced AX, a production-grade agent orchestration runtime with +2,305 stars in one day (Sep 2026 GitHub trending); positions as declarative agentic infrastructure.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — competing framework, not an adoptable pattern. AgentForge has its own orchestration model; adopting AX primitives would require architectural rewrite out of scope.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework (AutoGen folded in, April 2026)
summary: Microsoft moved AutoGen to maintenance-only and folded its capabilities into the unified Microsoft Agent Framework in April 2026; adds vector DB memory and parallel task execution by default.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge does not use AutoGen; parallel execution deliberately deferred. No actionable patterns.

source: Autonomous Event-Driven Multi-Agent Orchestration for Enterprise AI (arxiv 2606.20058)
summary: Proposes event-driven multi-agent orchestration where agents subscribe to streams and react asynchronously; benchmarks show throughput gains over sequential pipelines.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — parallel/event-driven multi-agent execution deliberately rejected in AgentForge for sequential determinism. Theme conflicts with core architecture decision.

source: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey (arxiv 2607.13104)
summary: Survey of self-improvement techniques from prompt tuning to workflow optimization to automated harness refinement; taxonomizes methods by scope (local step vs. global workflow) and supervision signal (execution trace, human feedback, model-as-judge).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — useful reference for the skill distillation direction. No gap it surfaces is untracked: HID-188 covers memory injection, existing distillationAgent.ts covers trace distillation. Backlog full.
